claims.claim_text: The indexed Brigadier General John Magruder is the career Army officer who headed the U.S. Military Mission to China before joining OSS.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact name and general-officer rank align with NARA's mission history and CIA's account of his China-to-OSS transition.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence: exact name, distinctive brigadier-general rank, China mission leadership, and official OSS role align.
claims.temporal_assessment: Official records document mission leadership in 1941-1942 and the summer 1942 OSS invitation.
claims.match_notes: The full service number remains private and is masked on the public profile.

claims.claim_text: Magruder's immediate pre-OSS assignment was leadership of the U.S. Military Mission to China.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NARA identifies Magruder as mission head; CIA states that this China role preceded his return and Donovan's invitation to join OSS.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence for the indexed brigadier general.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit immediate military-to-OSS sequence in official histories.
claims.match_notes: This is a military assignment, not a civilian employer.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Donald C. Downes is Donald Chase Downes, whose pre-OSS employment and intelligence chronology is documented by Yale.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact name and middle initial, Yale education, ONI work, and explicit OSS service align across the index and two institutional histories.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence: distinctive exact name plus matching official wartime intelligence chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Yale supplies a continuous sequence from 1940 intelligence work through the post-Pearl Harbor OSS appointment.
claims.match_notes: Postwar writing is used only for identity context and is not presented as pre-OSS employment.

claims.claim_text: Downes's immediate documented affiliation before OSS was employment by the Free World Association.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Yale places the employment after his ONI-directed return and immediately before stating that he joined OSS after Pearl Harbor.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence for Donald Chase Downes.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicitly sequenced as the final role before OSS, although exact appointment dates are not supplied.
claims.match_notes: The intelligence activity conducted from the position is noted without relabeling the organization as a government agency.

claims.claim_text: The Free World Association is Downes's last documented civilian employer before OSS service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Yale explicitly calls Downes an employee and then places his OSS entry after the Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence for Donald Chase Downes.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit immediate sequence in the institutional biography.
claims.match_notes: Robert College remains an earlier employer because later Free World Association employment intervened.

claims.claim_text: Downes taught English at Robert College in Turkey in 1940-1941.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Yale identifies the institution, teaching role, and concurrent use of the job as cover for intelligence activity.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence for Donald Chase Downes.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented pre-OSS employment superseded by a later civilian employer.
claims.match_notes: The cover function does not negate the documented employment relationship.

claims.claim_text: Downes held a reserve commission associated with the Office of Naval Intelligence before OSS.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Yale documents the reserve commission, Balkan intelligence work, and ONI order to return to the United States.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence for Donald Chase Downes.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented 1940-1941 military intelligence assignment before later civilian employment and OSS.
claims.match_notes: The military assignment remains separate from the concurrent Robert College teaching job.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Bruce C. Hopper is Harvard political scientist Bruce Campbell Hopper, whose World War II OSS work is documented by Harvard.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact name and middle initial, Harvard faculty career, Soviet expertise, and explicit OSS Stockholm service align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence: distinctive exact name plus an institutional biography explicitly documenting OSS service.
claims.temporal_assessment: Harvard documents his faculty appointment from 1930 through 1961 and wartime OSS service.
claims.match_notes: The indexed record has no rank; no military commission is inferred from his World War I service or wartime attaché title.

claims.claim_text: Hopper's best-supported immediate civilian affiliation before OSS was his Harvard University faculty appointment.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Harvard's chronology places his continuing associate professorship before and across his World War II OSS assignment.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence for Bruce Campbell Hopper.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded; the finding aid does not give the exact date on which wartime leave began.
claims.match_notes: The continuing appointment is modeled as employment and kept separate from the later government assignment.

claims.claim_text: Harvard University is Hopper's documented last civilian employer before wartime OSS service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Harvard records the faculty career and OSS assignment without identifying an intervening civilian employer.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence for Bruce Campbell Hopper.
claims.match_notes: Later Air Force consulting work is postwar and excluded.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Leopold 'Schwarsschild' is probably journalist and editor Leopold Schwarzschild, but the identity has not yet been confirmed from Box 690.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The name is highly distinctive, the spelling is a plausible index error, and the LBI chronology places Schwarzschild in the United States during the OSS period.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Probable: distinctive name and compatible chronology, but no second person-specific identifier appears in the index row.
claims.temporal_assessment: The LBI documents editorship through 1939 and U.S. emigration in 1940; the OSS personnel-file chronology remains unreviewed.
claims.match_notes: The historical spelling is added only as a documented candidate variant; the original indexed spelling remains the public heading.

claims.claim_text: If the identity match is confirmed, Schwarzschild edited Das Neue Tage-Buch in Paris from 1933 to 1939.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The Leo Baeck Institute provides the periodical title, role, location, and dates.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Probable rather than settled until the indexed personnel file is examined.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar work, ending before 1940 U.S. emigration; not shown to be immediately pre-OSS.
claims.match_notes: The claim is visibly conditional and excluded from default employer analytics.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Paul C. Child is Paul Cushing Child, the OSS graphics and presentation officer documented by CIA, NPS, and Harvard.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact name and middle initial, institutional wartime papers, official OSS identification, and China Theater role align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence: distinctive exact name plus multiple institutional sources explicitly documenting OSS service.
claims.temporal_assessment: Sources document prewar teaching and wartime OSS service, but not the exact appointment boundary.
claims.match_notes: The organizational word 'officer' is not treated as proof of a military commission.

claims.claim_text: Avon Old Farms School is Child's probable immediate civilian affiliation before OSS.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A reputable biographical account places his Avon teaching before wartime OSS service, but does not state a direct transfer.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence for Paul Cushing Child.
claims.temporal_assessment: Probable immediate sequence; the exact school departure and OSS entry dates require archival review.
claims.match_notes: The profile uses qualified language and excludes this affiliation from default high-confidence analytics.

claims.claim_text: Avon Old Farms School is Child's last currently documented civilian employer before OSS, with the chronology still requiring personnel-file confirmation.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The reviewed biography identifies Avon as his later prewar school employer; no later civilian employer has been established.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence for Paul Cushing Child.
claims.temporal_assessment: Probable last civilian employer, not yet explicit in a direct personnel or employment record.
claims.match_notes: This qualified claim is not counted as a verified employer in default analytics.
